question: How long does Manitoba health coverage generally continue after I permanently move to another Canadian province?
generated_answer:
You are covered for the balance of the month of departure, and the first two months following. You are also covered during a temporary absence to another province up to a maximum of 12 months. To ensure coverage, you should apply for out-of-country health insurance within two months of departure. After 12 months, you may be considered a resident of another province and would become eligible for coverage in that province. If you have not yet established residency in another province, you should apply for out-of-country health insurance. 3.3 Coverage During Temporary Absences in Canada

The Medical Services Insurance Regulation (M.R. 46/93, sub-section 2(1)) defines a "resident" of Manitoba as a person who is legally entitled to be in Canada, makes his or her home in Manitoba, is physically present in Manitoba for at least six months in a calendar year, and includes a person who is a temporary resident, within the meaning of the Inter-Provincial Agreement on Eligibility and Portability, who has not completed a total of 12 months of residence in Manitoba. Residents present in Manitoba on a temporary basis, such as vacationers or those present in Manitoba for a business trip, are considered residents of Manitoba. All residents are eligible for coverage under the health care plan. Section 3 of the Health Services Insurance Act provides that no resident of Manitoba shall be refused coverage by virtue of his or her financial status. The Medical Services Insurance Act, section 3, prohibits extra-billing by physicians. Manitoba Health has not received any reports of such activity. Insured physician services are paid at the same rate as those paid at the provincial level. Insured surgical services provided by physicians in Manitoba are paid at the same rate as those paid at the provincial level. 4.0 Accessibility

4.1 Access to Insured Health Services

Manitoba has no formal provisions to ensure access to insured health services based on such social factors as income, education, language, culture, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, social class, occupation, age, mental or physical disability or place of residence. 4.2 Access to Insured Hospital Services

As of March 31, 2005, Manitoba had 102 health facilities delivering insured hospital services to both in- and out-patients. This included 10 hospitals providing acute care services to both in- and out-patients, one hospital providing chronic care services to in-patients only, 76 personal care homes, 10 health centres and 5 special-care facilities. 4.3 Access to Insured Physician Services

As of March 31, 2005, there were 1,903 physicians licensed to practice in Manitoba, and of those, 1,562 (82.1 percent) were participating in the health care insurance plan. Certain physicians have opted out of the Medical Services Insurance Plan in accordance with section 91 of the Act. Manitoba Health is not required to provide compensation to opt-out physicians for services rendered to insured persons. As of March 31, 2005, there were 142 opt-out physicians in the province. Manitoba Health does not have any formal waiting time guarantees, except for medically required surgeries. However, Manitoba Health is committed to providing access to diagnostic services and treatment services within Manitoba's health system. 4.4 Physician Compensation

Manitoba Health and the Manitoba Medical Association (MMA) have a four-year Physician Master Agreement that was signed on February 18, 2005, and is effective April 1, 2005, to March 31, 2009. The Physician Master Agreement establishes the terms and conditions of payment to physicians for all insured services. The agreement also establishes the processes by which changes in the agreement may be made, including dispute resolution. The Minister of Health and the MMA also have a separate agreement covering the terms and conditions of the Alternative Payments Program (APP). The APP Agreement was signed on May 17, 2005, and is effective April 1, 2005, to March 31, 2009. A Physician Resource Planning Committee (PRPC) was established in 1995 to provide advice on physician resource planning and renewal.
